speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: asked	the Prime Minister whether the appointment of the new Attorney-General, to take effect on 14 January 2017, accords with Article 35 of the Constitution.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: My concern is actually regarding specifically section 35(4) of the Constitution.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I would like the Minister's comments on whether he feels that there is any issue with regard to the age of the new appointee.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Article 35(4) provides that the AG may be appointed for a specific period of time and it also says that, subject to his being removed, he shall vacate his office at the expiration of the period but subject as aforesaid, meaning subject to the removal clause, he should otherwise hold office until the age of 60 years.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Furthermore, the proviso to Article 35(4) states that "The President has a discretion if he concurs with the advice of the Prime Minister to permit an AG who has attained the age of 60 years to remain in office." So, my point is that the Article does not seem to contemplate the appointment of a new AG who is more than 60 years old to assume the post.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I think that would not be an accurate reading.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In fact, it would be quite an inaccurate reading.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: One, an appointment of an AG without a specific term.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That can only be done when the appointee is under 60 years of age.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In that first situation, the appointment ends when he reaches the age of 60.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And of course, in both cases, the Government may allow extensions beyond the age of 60 or beyond the specified term.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The proviso applies in one of those situations when a person below 60 has been appointed, and then he is allowed to carry on beyond 60.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Any other reading − looking for a reasonable word − would not make much sense because that would say that you can carry on beyond 60 but only if you have been appointed before you reach 60.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: At that time, the relevant provision stated age 55.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Mr Chan Sek Keong, who was AG as well as Chief Justice, was appointed in 1992 at the age of 54.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He was appointed for a two-year term past the age of 55.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And in 1994, that age in Article 35(4) was changed from 55 to 60.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And Mr Chan continued to hold the office past the age of 60 and he was re-appointed for a series of terms thereafter.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He was 63 when he was appointed for a term of two years, and 65 when he left office.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And we have had a number of AGs below the age of 60 who were appointed for a specified term: Mr Walter Woon, the current Chief Justice, Justice Steven Chong and Mr V K Rajah.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Ms Lim, you have already asked two clarifications.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, my question is whether the Government would, in good faith, to clarify this matter, apply to Court for an interpretation to see whether the Government's view is correct.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If the Member feels that there is something wrong, I would leave it to the Member to apply.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If the Member is right, a number of anomalies, of course, Justice Chao Hick Tin's appointment as AG would then have been not in order.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: You must read the Constitution with common sense. "The Attorney-General" − I am reading 35(4) − "may be appointed for a specific period" − and that is the term appointment − "and, if he was so appointed, shall, subject to clause (6), vacate his office − at the expiration of that period, but subject as aforesaid, shall otherwise hold office until he reaches the age of 60".

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, it clearly envisages two types of appointments.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And it is strange to ask the Government, which has taken a view and has taken advice from AGC: "I disagree with you and therefore would you apply to Court?"
